- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -0.33 or 0.33 in recent days), model frequently underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing or decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to recent sentiment-driven moves to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast with 3-period moving average of true values for stability.
